title: Pressing shift-Ff10 does not open the context menu
line: Shift+F10 now opens context menus like the Menu key: on selected desktop icons, on the empty desktop and on panel widgets.
explanation: Context menus opened from the keyboard only with the Menu key: Folder View opened an item's menu from its Menu key handler, and libplasma's ContainmentItem::keyPressEvent opened the desktop or focused applet's menu only for Qt::Key_Menu. Shift+F10, the standard replacement on keyboards without a Menu key, was handled in neither place and did nothing. ContainmentItem now treats Shift+F10 like the Menu key (sending the right-click trigger without the Shift modifier, so it matches the configured context menu action), and Folder View forwards Shift+F10 to its Menu key handler, which opens the item's menu or passes the key on to the containment when nothing is selected.

commits.message:
containmentitem: open the context menu with Shift+F10

Shift+F10, the usual replacement for the Menu key on keyboards without
one, did nothing on the desktop and in panels. Handle it like the Menu
key, so it opens the menu of the focused applet or of the containment.

BUG: 519354

containments/desktop: open the context menu with Shift+F10

Shift+F10, the usual Menu key replacement on keyboards without one, did
nothing in Folder View, so keyboard users couldn't open an item's menu.
Forward it to the Menu key handler, which opens it at the current item.

BUG: 519354

review.text: Minimal and idiomatic 2-line fix in FolderView.qml that forwards Shift+F10 in Keys.onPressed to Keys.menuPressed(event), matching the existing Keys.onEnterPressed pattern right above it. It properly preserves containment fallback when nothing is selected and avoids the non-reactive dir.hasSelection() binding issue present in the older open MR !4001. Before/after screenshots and keyboard/selection regression checks cleanly verify the behavior.

My earlier request is done: ContainmentItem now treats Shift+F10 like the Menu key, stripping Shift so the trigger matches, and the shots show the desktop menu with nothing selected and Kickoff's applet menu in the panel. The coordination request no longer applies under this brief. But the reporter asked for Shift+F10 on the panel to open the current item's menu, the same as the Menu key, and several panel items handle only Qt::Key_Menu themselves: Task.qml (Keys.onMenuPressed), the system tray's AbstractItem.qml (Key_Menu in Keys.onPressed), and Kickoff/Kicker delegates. For a focused task or tray icon, Shift+F10 is not handled, bubbles up to ContainmentItem, and opens the Task Manager or System Tray widget menu instead of the task's or icon's menu. So it now does something different from the Menu key there. Only Kickoff's button, which has no handler of its own, was tested.
changes: Make Shift+F10 reach the per-item Menu key handlers. Preferably do it in one place in libplasma: re-send Shift+F10 to the focused item as a Qt::Key_Menu key event before normal handling, e.g. in the containment view/window key handling or an event filter. That fixes Folder View, tasks, tray icons and Kickoff/Kicker items together and may make the FolderView.qml commit unnecessary. Otherwise, add Shift+F10 to Task.qml, systemtray AbstractItem.qml and the Kickoff/Kicker delegates.
Test Shift+F10 on a keyboard-focused task and a tray icon (Meta+Alt+P, then arrow keys) and show that the same menu opens as with the Menu key

history.text: Forwarding Shift+F10 to Keys.menuPressed in the GridView handler is correct and follows the file's own Enter-to-Return pattern, and the shots show the item menu opening. But it only covers Folder View items. When nothing is selected, onMenuPressed passes the event up and ContainmentItem::keyPressEvent opens the desktop menu only for Qt::Key_Menu, so Shift+F10 still does nothing there, where the Menu key opens the desktop menu. The reporter asked for Shift+F10 to behave like the Menu key on the panel and the desktop too. There is also already an open MR from another contributor (!4001) for the same bug, so this should go through that MR rather than a competing one.
changes: Also treat Shift+F10 like Qt::Key_Menu in libplasma ContainmentItem::keyPressEvent (or the equivalent shared place), so the desktop and panel context menus open when no item handles it, and test with nothing selected
Coordinate with plasma-desktop!4001: comment there with the rebase issue and the non-reactive dir.hasSelection() problem, or offer this approach there, instead of opening a parallel MR

history.summary: Added a libplasma commit so ContainmentItem treats Shift+F10 like the Menu key, which opens the desktop menu when nothing is selected and the focused applet's menu in panels. The Folder View commit is unchanged. All three cases were re-verified on a fresh master before and after.

answers.request: Also treat Shift+F10 like Qt::Key_Menu in libplasma ContainmentItem::keyPressEvent (or the equivalent shared place), so the desktop and panel context menus open when no item handles it, and test with nothing selected
answers.answer: Done in libplasma ContainmentItem::keyPressEvent: Shift+F10 now goes through the Menu key path. The synthesized right-click is sent without the Shift modifier, otherwise its trigger would be "RightButton;ShiftModifier" and would not match the context menu action. Tested on kdetest10 with nothing selected (desktop menu opens), with the panel focused through Meta+Alt+P (Kickoff's applet menu opens) and with an icon selected (item menu). F10 alone and Ctrl+Shift+F10 still do nothing, and all libplasma autotests pass.

answers.answer: Not done here: fixers can't write to invent, so the comment has to come from Niccolò. A draft for !4001 is in entry.json notes. It covers the rebase conflict with 69996be2af, the non-reactive dir.hasSelection() binding and the libplasma part the MR doesn't cover, and offers this approach. Our branches stay local, so nothing competes with the MR until he decides. Applying !4001 as-is wasn't an option because it no longer applies and fails after deselecting and reselecting an icon.
